newsitem.title: JAPAN: Forex market reflects Japan fundamentals - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Forex market reflects Japan fundamentals - MOF.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday that the current foreign exchange market situation reflects Japan's economic fundamentals.

Asked whether the currency market was in or out of line with Japan's economic fundamentals following a firming of the dollar after the release of Japan's "tankan" corporate survey on Wednesday, Mitsuzuka said:
"It is reflecting fundamentals. Our basic stance is to watch currency movements calmly and carefully."
Mitsuzuka said that a supplementary budget for this fiscal year ending March 1997 would not be submitted to an extraordinary session of parliament starting on Friday due to time constraints.
However, a extra budget needed to be formed to cover costs for projects like the reconstruction after the Kobe earthquake and would be drafted along with the full state budget for next fiscal year.
The budget for the next fiscal year is usually drafted by the end of December and submitted to a regular session of parliament in January.

Mitsuzuka said the government would decide whether to introduce economic stimulative steps after discussions within the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and between the LDP and two parties that are in a loose alliance with it.
The minister said that he would aim to settle a dispute with the United States over how to deregulate Japan's insurance market in ministerial-level talks scheduled for December 6-7.
"I hope to resolve the issue during these talks. I have told officials in charge of the negotiations that I strongly hope to settle the issue," he said.
"I have no intention of breaking the December 15 deadline (for settlement of the dispute)."
He said Japan's parliamentary schedule meant that he would not be able to hold another meeting with his counterpart U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky after December 7.
